This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The current bug report points out an issue in the method of DOMNodePointer (specifically around line 120) where the code incorrectly only considers Node.ELEMENT_NODE and Node.DOCUMENT_NODE as matching nodes for the node() node test. However, according to XPath semantics, the node() test should match all node types.

The problematic code snippet described is:

```
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
  return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE
    || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
```

And the fix suggested is:

```
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
  return true;
```

The failed test `testAxisPreceding()` checks the XPath expression `//location[2]/preceding::node()[3]`. The node() test in the preceding axis should match all node types, not just element and document nodes. Due to the existing restrictive matching in DOMNodePointer, this causes the test to fail.

The recent reports do not mention anything that conflicts with this; the one about BasicNodeSet relates to node sets but not node type matching. Thus, this strongly confirms the current bug report.

The key method where this bug lives likely handles determining whether a node matches a given node test type (node(), text(), processing-instruction(), etc.). This checking is probably done in DOMNodePointer around line 120 with a switch over node test types.

Summary diagnosis:
- The failing test uses a node() test in XPath which should match any node type.
- The current DOMNodePointer implementation only matches element or document nodes to node().
- This causes failure for nodes of other types in the preceding axis.
- Changing the node test case for node() to always return true fixes the issue.

The next step is to identify exactly the method in DOMNodePointer that contains this matching logic (likely around line 120) to confirm and pinpoint the location to fix.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
